1.

This is the first bail application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail to the applicant, who has been arrested in connection with Crime No. 126/2023 registered in Police Station Khadgawan Distt. Manendragarh-Chirimiri- Bharatpur Chhattisgarh for offence punishable under Section 376(2)(N) of Indian Penal Code and Sections 4 & 6 of POCSO Act.

entities.text: Police Station Khadgawan Distt. Manendragarh-Chirimiri- Bharatpur Chhattisgarh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 2. As per the prosecution case, the applicant has allured and sexually exploited the prosecutrix on the pretext of marriage and the prosecutrix has also delivered a baby which is at present 3 years of age.
Based on such allegation, the aforesaid offence has been registered.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime in question for which, he is in jail since 05.04.2023.

He submits that the first incident took place on 28.10.2018 and on that date, the age of the prosecutrix was about 17 years 2 months 12 days, the FIR has been lodged belatedly on 04.04.2023 and out of their live-in-relationship, a baby was also born who has completed the age of three years as on date.

He places reliance in the matter of Maheshwar Tigga vs. State of Jharkhand reported in AIROnline 2020 SC 743 and has drawn attention towards para 20 of the said judgment and submits that both the prosecutrix and applicant were in relation having a conscious and deliberate choice.

entities.text: Maheshwar Tigga vs. State of Jharkhand reported in AIROnline 2020 SC 743
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submits that Police has made a bias investigation only to attract the offence under the POCSO Act.

It is submitted that the first incident has been reported on 22.10.2018 but on such date, they did not develop any physical relation and their physical relation have been developed after the prosecutrix Satendra Singh vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149699645/
1 had attained the majority.

entities.text: prosecutrix Satendra Singh vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the said aspects, the applicant may be enlarged on bail.
4. The prosecutrix has appeared through video conferencing from concerned DLSA and has raised objection for grant of bail to the applicant.

5. Per contra, learned State counsel opposes the bail application and submits that the consent of the minor prosecutrix is immaterial and the case law which is relied upon by the applicant's counsel is misconceived as the matter Maheshwar Tigga (Supra) relates to the issue when both the prosecutrix and applicant were of grown-up age and had already attained majority.

She submits that the said observation which has been made by the Supreme Court after hearing a Criminal Appeal in a trial and at this juncture, the said case law does not help to the case of the petitioner.

6. Replying to the aforesaid submission by State counsel, counsel for the applicant submits that in an identical case, a Co-ordinate Bench vide MCRC No. 2720/2023 dated 19.06.2023 has granted bail to the accused therein only on the ground that the FIR has been lodged belatedly and the complainant had attained the majority when FIR was lodged.

7. State counsel further submits that referring to the objection of the co- ordinate Bench is only of the pursuasive value and in a rape case, only on the ground the FIR has been lodged belatedly is no ground for bail.

She further submits that the applicant has cheated to the prosecutrix on the pretext of marriage and has never solemnised the marriage so from the inception he has a mal-intention to make a relation, even the prosecutrix has delivered a baby and the applicant neglected the family.

She further submits that the applicant is a person of 34 years of age and he allured a minor prosecutrix so the manner in which such a grown up person cheated to prosecutrix and developed physical relation, therefore the present is not a fit case to grant bail to the applicant.
8.
Considering the submission of parties and also considering the allegation which is serious in nature, as also the age of the applicant, this Court is not inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is rejected.
